text.T003:
What happens when machines generate faster than people can understand and verify? And what
      changes when the software itself relies on model judgment?
text.T007:
I see the AI-assisted SDLC as structurally unbalanced where generation accelerates faster
        than human understanding, verification and ownership. More output can coexist with review
        queues, rework and fragile maintenance.
text.T009:
investigates this gap and how teams can rebalance
        generation, verification and ownership. It treats proposed responses as hypotheses to test
        in context.
text.T019:
studies what I call Thinking Systems: software in
        which consequential runtime responsibilities depend partly on probabilistic model judgment.
        This is where I see the fullest expression of today's AI potential — and some of its hardest
        engineering problems.
text.T020:
The controlled object is the software system. Its control perimeter also includes human
        roles, evidence, decision authority and corrective action. It needs development lifecycles
        and operating models suited to uncertainty. Much remains to develop and test.
